title: ALMA Observations of a Gap and a Ring in the Protoplanetary Disk around TW Hya
question: Does the TW Hya disk show a gap and ring in 336 GHz dust continuum, how do they relate to the CO snow line, and how depleted is CO in the disk?

data.angular_resolution: 0.37x0.31 arcsec (~20 AU) full; 0.32x0.26 arcsec (~15 AU) for >200 kλ

what.value: Dust temperature profile Td=22K(R/10AU)^-0.3 from model fit

evidence.loc: Dust Surface Density and Gap Parameters
evidence.quote: We adopt $T_{d}=22K(R/{\rm 10AU})^{-0.3}$, where $R$ is the disk radius, by fitting the model result in (cite: Andrews12)
assuming an inclination angle of $7^{\circ}$ and a position angle of $-30^{\circ}$
the abundance ratios of CO $: ^{13}$CO$=$67 $:$ 1 and $^{13}$CO $:$ C$^{18}$O$=$7 $:$ 1 (cite: Qi11)

recipe.method: CASA calibration, self-calibration, CLEAN imaging full data and >200 kλ data
Power-law plus Gaussian fit to high-frequency profile, add Gaussian deficit to full-data profile to recover missing flux
key_parameters: Gap edges 9-13 AU inner, 39-43 AU outer

recipe.goal: CO column density and gas-to-dust ratio
recipe.method: Three-zone radiative transfer for C18O+continuum, Tg from 13CO peak Tb, derive N_CO and compare with dust
assumptions: CO/H2 = 6e-5; isotopologue ratios from Qi11; uniform vertical Tg

evidence.quote: The gap and ring are located at around 25 and 41 AU from the central star
